subject: RateBlend pilot pricing — exec signoff requested (discount exception)
messages:
From: Emily Chang <emily.chang@rateblend.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask & SOW — RateBlend

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — team loved the latency profile. We have an early-stage pilot budget but need a very concessional price to get leadership to greenlight. High level: 6-month pilot, expected 3–5M tokens/month; pilot outcome could convert to $750k ARR if results look good.

Reality: to move forward we need about a 60% discount off list for the pilot (and a 3-month billing deferral). Attached is the SOW and expected usage cadence.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support that structure, or what the minimum asks from your side would be to make this live?

Attaching: RateBlend_SOW_v1.pdf

—Emily
Emily Chang
Head of ML Integrations, RateBlend
emily.chang@rateblend.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot ask & SOW — RateBlend — recommend exec signoff

Marissa / Naomi / Rishi — forwarding RateBlend's ask. Key points:
- Prospect requests ~60% discount for a 6-month pilot + 3mo billing deferral.
- Pilot usage ~3–5M tokens / month initially; potential uplift to $750k ARR if converted.
- They referenced strict procurement timelines (decision by month-end).

My read: this exceeds our RevOps guardrails (>50% discount + cash deferral). I have two recommendation options below for sign-off:

1) Conservative (preferred): 40% discount, monthly billing, 60-day credit hold, hard usage cap (3.5M tokens/mo) + rollout milestones tied to feature adoption.
2) Aggressive (sales-led): 55% discount for 6 months + 3mo deferred invoice, in exchange for a 12-month revenue commitment if converted (guaranteed minimum).

Attachments: proposal_rateblend_v2.pdf (commercial terms draft)

Requesting a VP/CFO signoff on the aggressive path if we proceed — this is time-sensitive. Naomi, please advise on finance tolerance; Marissa, advise on limit of commercial exceptions without exec approval.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask & SOW — RateBlend — recommend exec signoff

Karthik — thanks for the summary. My thoughts: 60% + deferral is outside what RevOps can approve. Per policy, commercial exceptions up to 35% can be routed through RevOps with documented guardrails (usage caps, clawback on conversion, and clear termination milestones). Anything above 35% requires VP/CFO review.

If Sales can get a written 12-month conversion commitment and include a minimum guaranteed MRR on conversion, I would be comfortable recommending up to 45% to the CFO — but we need the margin model showing contribution after variable costs.

Please add the following to the proposal before escalation:
- Explicit usage cap and overage rate
- Conversion triggers and measurement clause
- Proof of budget signoff timeline from RateBlend

I endorse pushing for the 40% (conservative) route unless Finance confirms net-positive contribution at higher discounts.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask & SOW — RateBlend — recommend exec signoff

Folks — finance here. We cannot endorse a 60% concession with a billing deferral without margin analysis. Please provide:
1) Forecasted token consumption per month (by week) for the 6-month pilot.
2) Proposed unit price after discount and the expected contribution margin per token (post-infra/compute allocation).
3) Clarify whether the deferred billing is paid at pilot end or amortized on conversion.

If the conversion guarantee is solid (signed 12-month commitment on conversion with a minimum ARR), we can model a deeper concession. Otherwise, limit to 30% with strict prepayment or escrow. Also request a clause protecting Redwood from unexpected burst usage.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Finance — Revenue & Billing
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask & SOW — RateBlend — recommend exec signoff

Quick note — I can negotiate a conversion clause: if they sign a 12-month contract after pilot, we secure a minimum monthly commitment that offsets ~60% of the pilot discount over year 1. That makes the math palatable for a 45% pilot discount. I'll ask Emily if they're open to a guaranteed ramp by month 3 and an NRR protection clause.

—Rishi
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vp_cfo@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot ask & SOW — RateBlend — recommend exec signoff

Thank you all — attaching updated commercial draft with proposed guardrails (usage cap, conversion clause, and payment schedule).

Next steps I am requesting:
- Naomi: quick margin check on the 45% vs 40% scenarios (I highlighted the sensitivity table).
- Marissa: if you can provisionally escalate to VP/CFO for the 45% path, please advise language for the memo.
- Rishi: please confirm you can secure the 12-month conversion guarantee during your next customer call.

If VP/CFO agrees, I will send the final commercial offer to RateBlend today. Please respond with APPROVE or DECLINE to keep the audit trail tidy.

Attachments: proposal_rateblend_v2.pdf

—Karthik
Senior Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
